Rede's second beta adds more than one Audiobookshelf account and a new first-run setup. It shares Ond's playback engine and look.

This is still an early beta. Keep your Audiobookshelf backups: Rede writes listening progress, finished status and bookmarks to your server. Please report problems with your OS, Rede and server versions, and steps to reproduce.

### Downloads

| File | For |
| --- | --- |
| `Rede-0.1.0-beta.2-macos-universal.dmg` (or `.zip`) | macOS 11 or later, Apple silicon and Intel |
| `Rede-0.1.0-beta.2-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | Linux on Intel/AMD, glibc 2.39 or newer |
| `Rede-0.1.0-beta.2-linux-aarch64.tar.gz` | Linux on ARM64, glibc 2.39 or newer |

On macOS, open the dmg and drag Rede to Applications. On Linux, unpack the archive and run `./install.sh`; it installs under `~/.local`. Linux needs PipeWire's library and an unlocked Secret Service keyring (GNOME Keyring or KWallet).

[Install and sign-in instructions](https://github.com/Solidsilver/ond/blob/rede-v0.1.0-beta.2/docs/rede/README.md).

### What's new

- Sign in to more than one Audiobookshelf account and switch between them from the foot of the sidebar. Each keeps its own library, downloads and progress; pending progress is sent before a switch.
- Settings › Sources lists your accounts and replaces the Account tab.
- A first-run sheet replaces the sign-in screen. After signing out of one account, it lists the others so you can go back to one still signed in.

### Beta limits

- Audiobookshelf 2.26 or newer; 2.36 or newer recommended.
- One account is shown at a time; there's no merged library across accounts yet.
- Linux uses username/password sign-in. Browser/OpenID sign-in, media keys and system now-playing controls are macOS-only for now.
- Output follows the system device. No in-app output picker yet.
- Local folders, podcasts and Windows bundles come later.
- No automatic update check yet. Later betas will be on this repository's releases page.
